claude.sample_unit: ChatGPT-generated discharge instruction outputs (30 per prompt type)

links.outcome: Accuracy and completeness of LLM discharge instructions against ERAS-derived 43-item benchmark
links.effect: No factual inaccuracies or harmful statements found in any output; completeness gaps, e.g., full antibiotic details in 25.0%, fibre reintroduction 41.7%, adaptation period 30.0%.
links.quote: An expert review, conducted using a structured benchmark form to record any concerns, revealed no factual inaccuracies, recommendations inconsistent with evidence-based guidelines, or potentially harmful instructions in any of the ChatGPT-generated outputs, regardless of the prompt type.

links.outcome: Accuracy of non-English (Polish) LLM output for patient discharge instructions
links.effect: Polish-language outputs had no factual inaccuracies or hallucinations found by expert review; some content omissions (antibiotics, diet detail).
links.quote: Notably, no evidence of hallucination was observed in ChatGPT-4.0 Omni (May 2024 release).

links.outcome: Effect of emotional prompt framing on completeness and accuracy of generated instructions
links.effect: No significant differences in completeness for any of 43 features (all p ≥ .05); relative effects near 0.50; tone changed markedly (CRI up to 5.28 vs 0 in 26/30 PP outputs).
links.quote: No statistically significant differences in completeness were found between outputs generated with EP-type prompts and those generated with PP-type prompts for any feature (all p ≥.05, Fisher’s exact test).

links.outcome: Relational/empathetic linguistic construction of outputs under emotional versus primary prompts
links.effect: Emotional prompts markedly increased relational language: 26 of 30 PP outputs had CRI 0.00, whereas EP outputs had CRI ranging 0.00–5.28.
links.quote: In contrast, 26 of 30 PP-type outputs showed CRI = 0.00, indicating an almost complete absence of lexically detectable relational features.

links.outcome: Completeness of LLM clinical content against ERAS guidelines
links.effect: Core domains 100% present, but full antibiotic details only 25.0%, fibre reintroduction 41.7%, adaptation period 30.0%, GI symptom monitoring 33.3%.
links.quote: Only 25.0% of outputs addressed full antibiotic prescription details, while specific dietary components (eg, vegetables, fruits, cereals) were each covered in fewer than 25.0% of cases.

unlisted_practices: Emotional prompting (EmotionPrompt) to alter tone of LLM-generated patient education

links.quote: The mean Cohen’s kappa coefficient (κ) calculated across all 43 detailed features was 0.859 (95% CI [0.841, 0.878]), indicating a very high level of agreement between experts.

links.effect: Moderate symptoms → primary care 85.0%; severe complications → surgical ward / clinic 98.3%; life-threatening symptoms → ED / 112 100.0.
links.quote: Wound care and physical activity guidance were nearly comprehensive across both prompt-generated output types, whereas return-to-work instructions and recommendations for managing moderate symptoms, such as low-grade fever, mild gastrointestinal disturbances, or non-severe pain requiring primary care consultation, appeared in 85.0% of cases.

links.effect: Overall EP 29.03 (SD 2.312) vs PP 28.50 (SD 2.446), p=0.414; relative effect 0.44 (95% CI 0.29–0.59).
links.quote: Importantly, the Brunner Munzel analysis of domain level completeness did not reveal statistically significant differences between PP and EP outputs, with relative effect estimates close to 0.50 across domains.

links.effect: 26 of 30 PP-type outputs showed CRI = 0.00; only four PP outputs had markers, maximum 3.14.
links.quote: In contrast, 26 of 30 PP-type outputs showed CRI = 0.00, indicating an almost complete absence of lexically detectable relational features.

links.outcome: ERAS benchmark completeness of discharge instructions
links.effect: Antibiotic details 25.0%, fibre reintroduction 41.7%, adaptation period 30.0%, GI/red-flag monitoring 33.3%, dietary product groups below 25%.
links.quote: Several elements were underrepresented, including full antibiotic prescription details 25.0%, gradual fibre reintroduction 41.7%, specification of an adaptation period 30.0%, monitoring of gastrointestinal or other red flag symptoms 33.3%, and individual dietary product groups each below 25%.

unlisted_practices: Emotional prompt augmentation to increase relational and motivational tone in LLM-generated discharge instructions

links.outcome: Completeness and accuracy of discharge instructions against ERAS guidelines
links.effect: Core domains were 100% complete with zero factual inaccuracies, but antibiotic details (25.0%), fiber reintroduction (41.7%), adaptation period (30.0%), and symptom monitoring (33.3%) were underrepresented across prompts.
links.quote: These findings indicate that, despite overall high completeness at the level of broad domains, the model frequently omitted clinically relevant details that are important for safe self-management, particularly in the areas of pharmacotherapy and structured dietary guidance.

unlisted_practices: Emotional prompt engineering (incorporating affective and motivational stimuli into prompts to enhance output completeness and relational communication quality)

screen.reason: The study directly compares two prompt engineering strategies (standard primary prompt vs. emotional prompt with motivational cues) for generating discharge instructions with ChatGPT-4o, assessing their effect on completeness, accuracy, and tone.
